\section[o amanhecer]{o amanhecer — the dawn, daybreak}

\label{lesson:PT-C275-amanhecer}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for gradually, then the Portuguese for little by little.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o amanhecer}
\textbf{o amanhecer} — \textquotedblleft{}the dawn, daybreak\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Saímos de casa ao amanhecer.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{We left home at dawn.}
\end{quote}

Also a verb: \emph{amanhece cedo no verão} — it gets light early in summer.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{amanhecer} is built on \emph{manhã} \textquotedblleft{}morning\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), from Vulgar Latin \emph{māneāna}, from Latin \emph{māne} \textquotedblleft{}in the morning\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{o amanhecer}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{o amanhecer}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{o amanhecer}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for gradually, then the Portuguese for little by little, then say \emph{o amanhecer} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does o amanhecer mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The dawn, daybreak\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[o entardecer]{o entardecer — the late afternoon, early evening}

\label{lesson:PT-C275-entardecer}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for little by little, then the Portuguese for the dawn.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o entardecer}
\textbf{o entardecer} — \textquotedblleft{}the late afternoon, early evening\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Ao entardecer, as pessoas passeiam junto ao rio.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{In the late afternoon people stroll by the river.}
\end{quote}

Also a verb: \emph{entardece} — the afternoon is ending.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{entardecer} is built on \emph{tarde} \textquotedblleft{}afternoon, late\textquotedblright{}, which comes from Latin \emph{tardē} \textquotedblleft{}slowly, late\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[o anoitecer]{o anoitecer — nightfall}

\label{lesson:PT-C275-anoitecer}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the dawn, then the Portuguese for the late afternoon.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o anoitecer}
\textbf{o anoitecer} — \textquotedblleft{}nightfall\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Chegámos à aldeia ao anoitecer.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{We reached the village at nightfall.}
\end{quote}

Also a verb: \emph{no inverno, anoitece cedo}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{anoitecer} comes down from Old Portuguese (EtymDB), built on \emph{noite} \textquotedblleft{}night\textquotedblright{}, from Latin \emph{nox, noctis} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.

\section[o crepúsculo]{o crepúsculo — the twilight}

\label{lesson:PT-C275-crepusculo}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the late afternoon, then the Portuguese for nightfall.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o crepúsculo}
\textbf{o crepúsculo} — \textquotedblleft{}the twilight\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
No crepúsculo, o céu fica cor de laranja.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{At twilight the sky turns orange.}
\end{quote}

A literary word for the half-light after sunset.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{crepúsculo} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{crepusculum} \textquotedblleft{}twilight\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.

\section[a véspera]{a véspera — the eve, the day before}

\label{lesson:PT-C275-vespera}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for nightfall, then the Portuguese for the twilight.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a véspera}
\textbf{a véspera} — \textquotedblleft{}the eve, the day before\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Na véspera do exame, não dormi nada.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The day before the exam I did not sleep at all.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Na véspera da partida} — the day before leaving.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{véspera} is inherited from Latin \emph{vespera} \textquotedblleft{}evening\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB): the evening before a feast became the day before it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
